title: Analyze transmitter hopping and receiver sync
description:
Analyze actual hopping order, equal-average frequency use by each transmitter, receiver synchronization and continuous-input behavior. Include pauses, restarts, denied opportunities, sparse allowed sets and fixed discovery or receiver-home traffic. Keep rendezvous selection distinct from a hopping sequence.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Read-only analysis of candidate behavior against primary sources. Do not invent a new hopping protocol, rewrite schedulers or self-approve legal pseudorandomness. Supply findings to human authority review and existing admission owners.
acceptance_criteria: Independent sequence reasoning and event traces expose every claimed hopping property and its assumptions. A channel list, hash histogram or aggregate network average cannot prove per-transmitter compliance. Identify unsupported properties and reviewer questions, including behavior under a continuous information stream.
